async/scope#

Structured lifetime for language futures.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let group is FutureGroup<int> = FutureGroup();
let first = Worker(id: 1).run();
let second = Worker(id: 2).run();

group.start(first);
group.start(second);
await group.wait();

Description#

Structured lifetime for language futures.

FutureGroup<T> owns the completion lifecycle of registered Future<T> values. start() registers and eagerly starts a future without taking it away from the caller. Registering the same future identity again is idempotent.

wait() seals the group, waits for every child and observes all failures. cancel() also seals it and requests cancellation of unfinished children; call wait() afterwards when using a group directly. Explicit cancellation accepts cancellation-only child outcomes, including children already settled by a prior await cancellation; real secondary cleanup failures remain reported. Without explicit group cancellation, a cancelled child remains a failure. Registration after sealing throws FinishedFutureGroup.

active() counts children whose success, failure or cancellation cleanup has not settled yet. It is an observation for supervision and diagnostics, not a polling substitute for wait().

Independent child failures are reported in registration order. The first is the primary failure and later failures remain ordered secondary diagnostics. Typed catches continue to see the unchanged primary error.

FutureScope<T,R> binds that group lifecycle to one async body. The body is invoked once, receives only the Supervising<T> capability and may register children without gaining a separate way to finish the group. The scope waits for every child before publishing the body result:

object Job {
    Job();
    async run() is int { 21; }
}

object Batch {
    Batch();

    async run(group is Supervising<int>) is int {
        group.start(Job().run());
        42;
    }
}

let scope is FutureScope<int, int> = FutureScope(action: Batch().run);
let answer = await scope.outcome();

If the body fails, or the caller cancels scope.outcome(), unfinished children are cancelled and their cleanup is awaited. The body failure remains primary; independent child cleanup failures are retained as ordered secondary failures.

One scope owns one homogeneous child result type. Nest another scope when one operation owns children of another type.
